page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is a KVM-based virtual machine instance featuring 40 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 4.8 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, relying instead on external storage solutions. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.hfg6.10xlarge in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1438.99 and a multi-core score of 38378.07. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 2133.36 GB/sec, which drops to 108.89 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write bandwidth of 48.09 GB/sec. In database and key-value operations, the instance handles 34.78 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 14249.04 on PassMark database operations. For lightweight machine learning, it processes 135M parameter LLM prompts at 1841.39 tokens per second, though performance scales down to 56.94 tokens per second for a 7B parameter model.

From a resource allocation perspective, the dedicated core model ensures consistent CPU performance without virtualization-induced noisy neighbor effects, making it a stable choice for compute-heavy workloads. However, the lack of bundled local storage requires users to provision external block storage, which may introduce latency and additional configuration overhead. The 1:4.8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offers a balanced profile for general-purpose enterprise applications, multi-threaded decompression tasks (demonstrated by a bzip3 multi-threaded speed of 166.28 GB/sec), static web serving, and relational database hosting.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring 40 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. It is configured with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.8 GB of memory per core, and operates on a KVM hypervisor. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, but offers a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. Performance benchmarks indicate solid multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 38378.07 and a PassMark CPU score of 34691.95. It handles memory-intensive tasks with a cached read bandwidth of 2133.36 GB/sec and processes 34.78 million Redis SET operations per second. Lacking local storage, it relies on network-attached storage. This instance is appropriate for multi-threaded data processing, database operations, and enterprise web serving.
